sections.html:
Warner Robins began as a railroad stop called Wellston and grew around Robins Air Force Base, which sits just east of the city line across U.S. 129 and supplies more than 25,000 military, civil service and contractor jobs. The city had 80,308 residents in 2020, with an estimate of 87,761 for 2025. It covers about 38 square miles, lies 20 miles south of Macon, and spreads across Houston and Peach counties.

Owners occupy barely over half the homes here, 53.5% for 2020 to 2024 against 65.2% nationally, so the city has a big rental market and a young population. Median household income is $66,970 across 31,930 households. In 2020, 34,191 housing units stood in the city, and 7.4% were empty.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $185,700, against $332,700 nationally.
  • Median gross rent: $1,212.
  • Residents 65 and older: 11.9%, compared with 18.9% nationally.

sections.h2: Which governments tax a Warner Robins house?
sections.html:
Houston County, the Houston County school system, the state and the City of Warner Robins each take a share. The county seat is Perry, and cities inside the county are Warner Robins, Perry, Centerville and part of Byron.

A smaller slice of Warner Robins lies in Peach County and is served by the Peach County School District, so owners with a Peach County parcel should ask the Peach County Tax Commissioner how their bill is handled.

  • Houston County Tax Commissioner, Warner Robins office: 202 Carl Vinson Parkway, Warner Robins, GA 31088; (478) 542-2110; weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Perry office: 201 Perry Parkway, (478) 218-4940.
  • Email for real property questions: taxquestions@houstoncountyga.gov.
  • Houston County Tax Assessors, 201 Perry Parkway in Perry: (478) 218-4750 for real estate, with parcel data on qPublic.
  • City of Warner Robins billing questions: (478) 929-1148.

The assessors do not handle billing, and the commissioner does not set value or millage. Call the one that matches your question, and write down the name of the person you reach and the date of the call, which helps if a figure is questioned later at closing.

The Mayor and Council adopted 10.000 mills for the 2026 tax year, up 1.047 mills from the 8.953 rate used in 2024 and 2025, as the city announced. County and school rates are separate and appear on your own statement.

Houston County mails real estate statements ahead of October 20, and December 20 is the due date. The office accepts partial payments. Interest builds each month at the legal rate, and every 120 days adds a 5% penalty until the penalties reach 20%.

A lien may be recorded once tax is more than 90 days overdue, while a levy is held back as a last resort. Manufactured homes keep their own calendar: January bills, April 1 due date, decal on payment, and a 10% penalty for late payment.

Statements are mailed to the homeowner and never to the lender. Borrowers who escrow need to send the bill along themselves.

New homestead filings go to the Houston County Tax Assessor's Office and must arrive by April 1. First-time owners should bring a copy of the warranty deed. Once approved, the exemption continues until ownership or residence changes.

  • Age 65 and older, combined with another homestead exemption: relief from the state portion of tax on the house and as much as 10 acres.
  • Gross household income of $15,000 or less, age 62 and up: tax deferral.
  • Real property returns and conservation-use requests: mailed, with a postmark of April 1 at the latest.

To challenge a value, write to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice. From there the path runs through the Board of Equalization (or arbitration) and, if needed, Superior Court. Complaints about the size of the bill are outside the appeal.

Call the commissioner's Warner Robins office for a payoff and hand the figure to your closing attorney or title company. Value is fixed as of January 1 each year, so the sale contract should state how the year's bill is divided.

Landlords should check personal property too. People who buy a business, boat or aircraft sometimes find years of unpaid tax afterward, and attorneys usually review only the real estate side.

If you inherited the house, fell behind or live elsewhere, a buyer taking the house as it is can pay the county out of the proceeds, with no repairs or showings on your end.

A simple order of work: get the payoff, confirm your exemption status with the assessors, tell the title company whether any part of the lot falls in Peach County, and agree in the contract on who covers the current year's bill. Bring your deed and a photo ID to the counter if you go in person, and ask for the payoff figure by email so it is on paper for the closing.

sections.h2: What to check before you list
sections.html: Pull the parcel on qPublic and confirm the owner name, acreage and any homestead flag match what you expect. If the house sits near the city line, make sure you know which county and school district it belongs to, because that decides which office sends the bill. Rental owners should also confirm they have not skipped a return for any equipment kept at the property. Clearing these items before you list keeps a closing from stalling over a small record error, and it gives a buyer's agent one clean set of answers when they ask what the yearly bill has been.

Each bill combines several levies, and it helps to know which office stands behind each line. The county, the school system and the state have their own rates, and the city adds its mills on top for parcels inside Warner Robins. If you question the value, that is the assessors. If you question the arithmetic or the balance, that is the commissioner.

Because value is fixed as of January 1, a house that you improve in the spring is not reassessed for that year, and a house that burns or is damaged still carries the January value. Raise any change in condition with the assessors early so the record is right before you list.

Landlords who hold several parcels should ask the commissioner for a single list of open balances. It saves a trip and keeps one forgotten parcel from showing up at the closing table of another. Ask whether any parcel has a manufactured home or other personal property attached, since those accounts run on their own calendar and are easy to overlook.

faqs.q: What is the due date for property tax in Warner Robins?
faqs.a: December 20. Statements go out before October 20, and manufactured homes are billed separately for April 1.

faqs.q: What millage did Warner Robins adopt for 2026?
faqs.a: 10.000 mills, up from 8.953 mills in both 2024 and 2025.

faqs.q: Where can I pay in person in Warner Robins?
faqs.a: At the Houston County Tax Commissioner's office, 202 Carl Vinson Parkway, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. An online payment adds a convenience fee.

faqs.q: Who reviews a Houston County value dispute first?
faqs.a: The Board of Tax Assessors, reached at (478) 218-4750 for real estate. The notice gives you 45 days.

faqs.q: Do Peach County parcels in Warner Robins go to Houston County?
faqs.a: No. That slice of the city is served by Peach County's offices, so ask the Peach County Tax Commissioner how the parcel is billed.
